summary.reasoning: the retry guard holds on the parity path only; the live path still re-enqueues.

findings.title: test over-specifies the ordering
findings.body: asserts exact call order where the contract only promises the set.

findings.title: retry fix is parity wiring, not a live fix
findings.fix: move the retryable check ahead of the parity branch
findings.body: the guard only runs on the parity path; the live path still re-enqueues a permanently failed job.
findings.evidence:
FAIL queue/enqueue.test.ts > live path drops permanent failures
  expected enqueue calls: 0
  received enqueue calls: 1

findings.title: README still says delay
findings.fix: say backoff in the README and name the base interval and the cap it grows to
findings.body: the README describes a fixed delay; the queue now backs off exponentially.

findings.title: permanent failures re-enqueue forever
findings.fix: drop non-retryable jobs in the worker's catch block
findings.body: a job marked retryable: false goes back on the queue after every failure, so it never leaves.

findings.title: the backoff schedule doubles from a 250 ms base with ±20 % jitter per attempt, so the tenth retry already waits past four minutes, which outlasts the worker lease; renew the lease on each attempt or cap the schedule below it
findings.body: the 300000 ms cap appears inline with no name, and nothing ties it to the lease.

strengths.lead: the retry test names its contract
